answer: Sybil defense can rely on proof-of-personhood, not self-declared identity. Suppose a bot runs an onyx pattern: it creates ten thousand wallets, each posing as an independent agent. Every agent needs a scarce external anchor, a unique verified human or hardware enclave that sponsors one actor. Duplicates collapse onto one root, so thousands of wallets yield one weight unit. The cost is anchors, not compute: distinct anchors need real resources and carry revocation risk. Staking adds a wall, since each agent locks collateral in a garden and cheating is slashed. Quartz attestations block replay.
